title: GDPR: free movement of personal data within the Union neither restricted nor prohibited
publisher_or_author: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
claim: Article 1(3) of the EU General Data Protection Regulation provides that the free movement of personal data within the Union shall be neither restricted nor prohibited for reasons connected with the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data.
evidence_summary: Article 1(3) GDPR establishes that free movement of personal data within the Union may not be restricted or prohibited on data-protection grounds, i.e. the GDPR does not permit data-localisation barriers to intra-Union transfers of personal data.
source_excerpt: The free movement of personal data within the Union shall be neither restricted nor prohibited for reasons connected with the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data.
interpretation: Normative evidence of the EU legal position on data localisation: a statutory prohibition on restricting or prohibiting the free movement of personal data within the Union for data-protection reasons. Establishes that the EU framework does not impose territorial data-storage mandates for intra-Union transfers; used as a comparator for Ethiopia's territorial storage mandate under PDP 1321/2024 Art. 22.
methodology_or_basis: Direct quote of Article 1(3) of the regulation text.
keywords: GDPR, free movement of personal data, data localisation, European Union
